_note: Dashboard-owned deal READS (interpretation the engine never writes). Generated from the payload only — never the web — by scripts/generate_reads.mjs, following .claude/skills/capital-flow-reads, on the weekly run. KEYED BY the engine's stable flow.id ('flow:...'): a read is written once per id and only regenerated for new ids, so unchanged deals are never re-worded. Legacy entries keyed 'alloc:...=>target:...' are pre-id-cache hand notes and still resolve. The adapter's flowNote() prefers an engine-emitted flow.read if one ever ships. Value shape: {angle, read}. UI labels every non-engine read 'наша трактовка · не данные движка'.

flow:08b533b9a0869eac.read: Blackstone размечает программу дата-центров в Японии на $30 млрд — единолично, через проектное финансирование. Тезис управляющего: владеть цифровой инфраструктурой в дефицитных по мощности географиях с контрактным арендным потоком. Пока кандидат — программа заявлена, но сделки ещё предстоит подтвердить.

flow:09474f5dbadfc0c5.read: США участвуют грантом на $17.5 млрд в развёртывании реакторов Westinghouse вместе с Brookfield и Cameco — государственные деньги заходят в атом как длинная ставка на энергию для AI. Подтверждено. Редкий случай прямого государственного капитала в энергетическом хребте стройки.

flow:1df0c445ffa48c84.read: KKR закрывает пятый флагманский инфраструктурный фонд на $19.2 млрд — сухой порох под core-plus активы, всё чаще с уклоном в цифровую инфраструктуру AI. Не сделка, а запас капитала, который проявится позже отдельными чеками. Подтверждено.

flow:304a1412c9cbb7b9.read: Крупнейший выкуп вне AI на карте: Saudi PIF ведёт поглощение Electronic Arts вместе с Silver Lake и Affinity, а долг берёт на себя JPMorgan. Для суверенного фонда это ставка на интерактивные развлечения как стратегический актив, а не на инфраструктуру. Напоминание, что национальный капитал аллоцирует широко, а не только в дата-центры.

flow:3d6815efc500cbe3.read: NVIDIA не строит и не покупает — она подписывается гарантом почти на $250 млрд, чтобы OpenAI смогла арендовать площадку на 10 ГВт у SB Energy. Ставка на спрос: чем больше OpenAI развернёт, тем больше систем NVIDIA закупит проект (в рамках сделки, способной превысить $500 млрд с учётом финансирования чипов). Пока это кандидат — структура ещё оформляется, но масштаб задаёт потолок всей карте.

flow:486b85d8c0f7b81b.read: Amazon доливает $10 млрд в Anthropic — параллельно своей же доле в OpenAI, страхуя ставку сразу на две фронтир-лаборатории поверх AWS. Подтверждено. Для Anthropic это капитал под обучение следующего поколения моделей и аренду мощности.

flow:4b40ff33c0f516ae.read: Sequoia участвует в Series H Anthropic вместе с Altimeter, Greenoaks, Coatue, Capital Group и другими — верхушка венчура и кроссовер-фондов в одной строке. Оценка приблизительная, статус кандидат: раунд ещё оформляется. Сигнал сходимости умных денег на одной цели.

flow:4c0f370abfa063c0.read: Amazon доливает в OpenAI в раунде, где рядом NVIDIA, SoftBank, Microsoft, a16z и D. E. Shaw — редкий случай, когда конкурирующие гиганты сидят в одной таблице капитализации. Для Amazon это доступ к фронтир-модели поверх собственного облака. Подтверждено на 100 — раунд закрыт.

flow:70df690be1075b1a.read: Крупнейшая подтверждённая стройка карты: Brookfield берёт под контроль кампус на бывшей урановой площадке DOE в Кентукки (1.2+ ГВт под вычисления), а NextEra строит выделенную генерацию на 4.6 ГВт. Фирменный тезис Brookfield — владеть инфраструктурным «хребтом» AI с контрактным денежным потоком, а не гадать, чья модель победит. Читается насквозь до поставщиков турбин, батарей и распредустройств.

flow:7f35b0a50d0c21ed.read: MGX (ОАЭ) поднимает флагманский фонд на $49 млрд под весь AI-стек — от вычислений до приложений — привлекая LP из Залива, Северной Америки, Азии и Европы. Это не сделка, а запас капитала, который затем растечётся по десяткам целей. Госденьги задают темп, за которым идут остальные.

flow:801b9e89564b2f57.read: Anthropic сама подписывается под $19 млрд долга, чтобы законтрактовать мощность кампуса TeraWulf в Кентукки — лаборатория покупает не железо, а гарантированную ёмкость под инференс. Оценка приблизительная, но статус подтверждён. Показатель того, что фронтир-лабы всё чаще финансируют собственную инфраструктуру напрямую.

flow:87ae55925a00cf1a.read: Meta финансирует Hyperion — свой крупнейший обучающий кластер на 5 ГВт ИТ-мощности — сама, с баланса, без соинвесторов. Фирменный стиль Цукерберга: не доли в чужих лабах, а собственные мегакампусы под «личный суперинтеллект». $50 млрд здесь — это capex, который придётся залить в бетон и подключить к сети.

flow:ba18efd3d5bbd41e.read: Korea Investment Corporation открывает стратегический счёт на $14 млрд под AI, дата-центры и стратегические отрасли — суверенный сухой порох, а не отдельная сделка. Национальный капитал резервирует позицию в гонке за вычислениями. Пока кандидат.

flow:e4952eba0379e007.read: Оборотная сторона Hyperion: Blue Owl структурирует финансирование расширения до 5 ГВт, где Meta держит лишь ~20%. Тот же объект, что и подтверждённый поток Meta, но другой карман — так гиперскейлер снимает многомиллиардную стройку со своего баланса. Статус кандидат: структура ещё оформляется.

flow:ecad0271aefe8c4b.read: Meta заходит на $9.2 млрд в кампус в Стерджен-Каунти (Альберта) — единолично, с баланса, расширяя парк гиперскейл-дата-центров за пределы США. Оценка приблизительная, но подтверждено. Тот же паттерн: собственный бетон под собственные модели, теперь в дешёвой по энергии Канаде.

flow:f53b2b79dd744f2d.read: Ex-Im Bank США открывает экспортно-кредитную линию на $15 млрд под стратегические инвестиции Saudi PIF — политически окрашенный капитал, привязывающий американских поставщиков к суверенным проектам. Статус кандидат (70): структура заявлена, но не закрыта. Показывает, как переплетаются госкапитал и геополитика.

alloc:Altimeter=>target:Thrive Holdings.read: Thrive buys traditional IT and accounting firms and rewires them with AI — margin expansion on acquired revenue rather than a product launch. If it works it is the cleanest way to monetize models without owning one; the strategic stake behind it tells you who supplies the intelligence.

alloc:Andreessen Horowitz=>target:Atoms.angle: Robots as labour, sold by the hour
alloc:Andreessen Horowitz=>target:Atoms.read: Kalanick's industrial-robotics company aims at food, mining and transport — physical work priced per task rather than hardware sold per unit. $1.7B at this stage is a factory bet, not a software bet: the risk sits in capex and uptime, not model quality.

alloc:Andreessen Horowitz=>target:Cathed.read: Ex-government staff building AI-powered military cyber capability — a category where the buyer is a state and the moat is clearance, not code. a16z and Sequoia entering together mirrors the defense playbook that already worked twice this decade.

alloc:Andreessen Horowitz=>target:Etched.read: The other half of Etched's round. a16z runs the full AI stack, so silicon is the hedge against value concentrating in models it does not own. Two brand-name leads on identical terms compresses the window for anyone else to get in.

alloc:BlackRock=>target:Aligned Data Cen.angle: Buying the landlord, not the tenant
alloc:BlackRock=>target:Aligned Data Cen.read: The largest single flow on the map, and it buys capacity rather than models. BlackRock's infrastructure arm takes control of an AI-ready developer-operator across the Americas — the pick-and-shovel position where the return is contracted rent, not an option on which lab wins. The read-through runs straight to the power, cooling and switchgear suppliers those campuses have to order from.

alloc:BlackRock=>target:Meta El Paso dat.angle: Hyperscaler capex, moved off balance sheet
alloc:BlackRock=>target:Meta El Paso dat.read: A 1GW campus built for a single occupant, with BlackRock-managed funds holding 80% and Meta 20%. Meta gets the compute without the capex line; BlackRock gets a long-dated lease against one of the strongest tenant credits in tech. Expect the structure to be copied — it converts AI buildout into an investable, bond-like asset.

alloc:Blackstone=>target:Japan AI data c.read: Retired LCD and fab plants come with the two things a greenfield site cannot buy quickly: heavy grid connections and industrial zoning. Blackstone underwrites the Japanese leg of the buildout on that arbitrage. Status is candidate — treat the size as directional until a primary source lands.

alloc:Blackstone=>target:QTS Realty Trus.read: Blackstone funds the next build phase of a hyperscale operator it already owns — capital recycling inside the house rather than a new position. Read it as a demand signal: the incremental dollar goes to AI-ready campuses, and QTS's leasing pace is the tell for whether hyperscaler appetite is still running ahead of supply.

alloc:Blue Owl=>target:Kirkwood Infrastr.read: Compute clusters are worth little unstitched. Blue Owl seeds a fiber-and-conduit platform to own the connectivity backbone between AI campuses — the least glamorous, most toll-like layer of the stack. The SPV wrapper signals a build-and-hold asset, not a flip.

alloc:Brookfield=>target:Bloom Energy.read: Interconnect queues, not GPUs, now set the pace of the buildout. Brookfield underwrites on-site solid-oxide generation so campuses can energize ahead of the utility — buying years, which is the scarcest input in this cycle. Project-finance structure means the return is contracted cash flow rather than a levered call on AI demand.

alloc:Coatue=>target:Coatue Retail Fund.angle: Retail capital enters the private AI trade
alloc:Coatue=>target:Coatue Retail Fund.read: Coatue's first retail-facing crossover vehicle, aimed at public tech and late-stage private AI. The structure matters more than the size: when a private-market trade is opened to retail, the institutional entry is already behind us. Worth tracking as a cycle marker.

alloc:Coatue=>target:Databricks.angle: Own the data layer, not the model
alloc:Coatue=>target:Databricks.read: Models commoditize; the governed enterprise data they are trained and served on does not. A $3B late-stage cheque is a bet that the lakehouse becomes the control point for corporate AI — and a pre-listing position in the most obvious IPO candidate in the stack.

alloc:Coatue=>target:Norm Ai.read: Coatue joins Khosla on the same round. Public-market crossover funds moving this far down-stage is a familiar late-cycle pattern: capital chasing an entry point before the listed comparables reprice.

alloc:DigitalBridge=>target:Nippon Gatew.read: DigitalBridge buys into Japan through NEC's data-center assets in Greater Tokyo and Osaka — sites with power and permits already attached in a market where new grid capacity is effectively rationed. The scarce asset here is the connection, not the shell. First mover on the sector's smart-money cluster this cycle.

alloc:Elad Gil=>target:Odyssey.angle: World models as the next modality
alloc:Elad Gil=>target:Odyssey.read: Odyssey trains real-time world models — video you can act inside rather than watch. Gil moving first here is what the engine flagged as smart money; two allocators followed within three weeks. The founders come out of self-driving, where real-time simulation was the hard-won skill.

alloc:Eric Schmidt=>target:General Intui.read: Schmidt's cheques cluster where AI meets physical and strategic capability, and he lands here alongside Bezos. Two allocators of this weight on one early cap table says more about the data asset than about current model quality.

alloc:Galaxy Digital=>target:Galaxy Heli.read: Phase two of converting a West Texas crypto site into AI/HPC capacity anchored by CoreWeave. The trade is the interconnect: hundreds of megawatts already energized for mining are worth far more serving inference. The cleanest example on this map of stranded power being repriced by AI demand.

alloc:Garry Tan=>target:Monogram.read: Monogram generates interactive visual interfaces instead of returning text — a wager that the chat window is a transitional UI. Small and early, but interface resets are what decide which layer of the application stack accrues the value.

alloc:Garry Tan=>target:Odyssey.read: YC's president joining after Gil's lead is exactly the clustering this map exists to catch — conviction propagating through one network before the round is fully priced. On its own a small cheque; as the second name on the same cap table inside 21 days, a position signal.

alloc:Jeff Bezos=>target:CuspAI.read: Materials discovery is the highest-leverage non-language application: better sorbents, catalysts and batteries compound into every physical industry. Backing an AI materials foundry is the same thesis as the robotics cheques in this book, one layer further upstream.

alloc:Jeff Bezos=>target:Flourish.angle: Attacking the energy cost of inference
alloc:Jeff Bezos=>target:Flourish.read: A brain-inspired compute architecture aimed at the one number that decides how far AI spreads: joules per token. Take inference energy down an order of magnitude and whole classes of application become viable — the same argument that makes inference silicon the crowded trade this cycle.

alloc:Jeff Bezos=>target:General Intuiti.read: A lab spun out of a gaming-clip platform, training agents on spatial-temporal reasoning from human play — a data source no frontier lab can simply scrape. Bezos and Schmidt entered the same round, which is the convergence the engine lit up in AI Labs this cycle.

alloc:Jeff Bezos=>target:Generalist AI.read: Foundation models for dexterous manipulation that run on anyone's robot — the Android strategy for embodied AI, against the vertically integrated approach. Third robotics-adjacent name in the same book, which makes it a thesis rather than a punt.

alloc:Jeff Bezos=>target:Prometheus.read: Heavily capitalized and deliberately quiet — models built to understand the physical world for industrial use. The portfolio pattern is clear: language is assumed, and the frontier being funded is embodiment. Unconfirmed status; the size is what would matter if it firms up.

alloc:Khosla Ventures=>target:Norm Ai.angle: Compliance is the sharpest agent wedge
alloc:Khosla Ventures=>target:Norm Ai.read: Norm turns regulation into executable compliance agents — a domain where output is auditable, the buyer already holds the budget line, and errors get caught by design. Exactly the shape of AI application that survives enterprise procurement.

alloc:Meta=>target:Meta-BlackRock El Pas.angle: The other side of the JV
alloc:Meta=>target:Meta-BlackRock El Pas.read: Meta's 20% of the vehicle that owns the campus Meta will fully occupy. Holding the site through a JV rather than as owned capex keeps the Sopaipilla notes off the corporate balance sheet while Meta still controls the compute. The same asset appears twice on this map — once from each partner.

alloc:NVIDIA=>target:Safe Superintellige.read: NVIDIA takes a stake in a lab whose entire cost base is NVIDIA silicon. Strategically it locks in a frontier design partner; financially it is the circularity the market keeps flagging — revenue and investment travelling the same loop. Small against NVIDIA's cash, large as a signal of where the next architecture gets shaped.

alloc:Peter Thiel=>target:Etched.read: Etched burns the transformer straight into the die — no generality, enormous throughput per watt on the one architecture that matters. The bet is that this cycle's economics shift from training runs to serving tokens, and that as token cost falls, demand expands faster than general-purpose GPUs can absorb it. Whoever owns the cheapest inference stack captures that expansion — and three separate allocators on this map are already in the name.

alloc:Peter Thiel=>target:Founders Fund.angle: Dry powder ahead of the round
alloc:Peter Thiel=>target:Founders Fund.read: The firm's largest vehicle, aimed at late stage rather than seed — a view that this cycle's winners are already identifiable and simply need capital to stay private longer. Fund launches are the leading indicator on this map: money committed here reappears as deals two to six quarters out.

alloc:Peter Thiel=>target:Panthalassa.read: Wave-powered floating platforms running AI compute at sea — a direct answer to the two hard constraints on land, grid interconnect and permitting. Classic long-horizon shape: a physical, jurisdiction-light bet rather than another application-layer round. Unconfirmed, and the engineering risk is the whole story.

alloc:Reid Hoffman=>target:Prentis.angle: Agents that use software like people do
alloc:Reid Hoffman=>target:Prentis.read: Computer-use models driving browser, desktop and mobile — the wrapper that turns a model into labour without waiting for every vendor to ship an API. Hoffman's cheques track the enterprise-adoption path; this is a bet on where agent value actually lands.

alloc:Sequoia=>target:Cathedral.read: Sequoia matches a16z into the same round. Two firms of this size splitting a $160M cheque suggests the constraint is contract timing rather than conviction — the value accrues when programme-of-record budget lands.

alloc:Sequoia=>target:Etched.angle: The priced round behind the crowd
alloc:Sequoia=>target:Etched.read: Sequoia and a16z co-anchor $300M into the inference-ASIC bet the individual allocators are also chasing. When the venture majors and the family offices converge on one name inside a single cycle, the scarce input is allocation, not capital.

alloc:Sequoia=>target:Valar Atomics.read: Small modular reactors sold to compute and industry — the only supply that scales with demand instead of queuing for the grid. A billion at this stage prices in regulatory success, which is the real variable. Sits directly upstream of every datacenter flow on this map.

alloc:SoftBank=>target:OpenAI.read: SoftBank doubles down on the single position that now defines its book. At this size it stops being a venture bet and becomes an index on frontier-model economics — if inference margins compress there is no diversification behind it. It also buys strategic proximity to the compute programme SoftBank is financing on the other side of this map.

alloc:Stanley Druckenmiller=>target:Etch.angle: A macro investor on a private cap table
alloc:Stanley Druckenmiller=>target:Etch.read: Druckenmiller does not usually appear this early, which is the point. It reads as a levered private expression of a view he can only blunt in public markets: compute demand keeps outrunning supply, and the margin migrates to whoever serves inference cheapest.
